open: In the name of Allah. Assalamu alaikum, my dears. Come closer, tonight’s story is very beautiful.
s1a: Have you ever been thirsty, really, really thirsty? Imagine a very hot desert, with no water anywhere… and suddenly a spring gushes up from the sand! A spring that is still there today!
s1c: Really, my dear. Get warm and cosy… Tonight I’ll tell you about the Prophet Ismail, peace be upon him, the son of Ibrahim.
s2a: When Ismail was still a nursing baby, Allah gave Ibrahim a command. Ibrahim brought Ismail and his mother Hajar to a valley where, on that day, there was no one, and no water.
s2b: Hajar said: O Ibrahim, where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no person and nothing? Then she said: Is it Allah who commanded you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us be lost.
s2d: She trusted Allah, my dear. And Ibrahim prayed to his Lord: “Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in an uncultivated valley near Your sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among the people incline toward them and provide for them from the fruits that they might be grateful.”
s3a: Hajar had a bag of dates and a waterskin with water. When the water in the waterskin ran out, she became thirsty, and her son Ismail became thirsty.
s3b: She saw him twisting and turning, and she went away because she could not bear to watch him. She climbed Safa and looked: could she see anyone? She saw no one. Then she went to Marwah and looked: could she see anyone? She saw no one.
s3c: She did that seven times. Do you know what? Our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “That is the going of the people between them.” That means: people go between Safa and Marwah, just as Hajar did.
s4a: When she reached the top of Marwah, she heard a voice… and there was the angel, at the place of Zamzam. He dug the ground with his heel, or with his wing, until the water appeared.
s4b: Hajar began to make a little basin around it, and to scoop water into her waterskin. She drank, and she nursed her child.
s4c: Zamzam! I know that water! People drink it in Makkah!
s4d: That’s the very one, my dear, and it still flows today. And the angel said to Hajar: Do not be afraid of being lost, for here is the House of Allah, which this boy and his father will build, and Allah does not let His people be lost.
s5a: Then some people from the tribe of Jurhum passed by. They saw a bird circling above the valley and said: This bird must be circling over water, but we know this valley, and there is no water in it. They came and said to Hajar: Will you allow us to settle near you? She said: Yes. So they settled there, until there were several families of them in the valley.
s5b: Ismail grew up among them, and he learned Arabic from them. And Allah says in the Qur’an: “And mention in the Book, Ismail. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.”
s6a: Then Ibrahim came and said: O Ismail, Allah has given me a command. He said: Do what your Lord has commanded you. He said: And will you help me? He said: I will help you. He said: Allah has commanded me to build a House here. So Ismail brought the stones, and Ibrahim built, and both of them were saying: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing.”
s6c: Yes, my dear, that is the Kaaba in Makkah. Wherever Muslims are, they turn towards it in their prayer, and so do we when we pray.
s7a: Oh… they’ve fallen asleep. My dears… trust Allah like Hajar, for Allah does not let His people be lost. Do your best, just as she went back and forth between Safa and Marwah. Keep your promises like Ismail. And when you do something good, say: Our Lord, accept it from us.
s7b: And next time, I’ll tell you about Ishaq, Ismail’s brother, and about amazing good news that came to an old woman. And you, watching us right now: if you liked the story, ask your parents to subscribe to our channel, so you don’t miss the next story.
close: And you, dear fathers and mothers: subscribe to our channel, and share these stories with the people you love, so that together we pass on the beautiful message of Islam to our children.
final: Good night, my dears. I entrust you to Allah, with whom nothing entrusted is ever lost.
